_doc: Headwaters source registry for Surat (city 9, first Gujarat city).
The registry OWNS licence strings: NVDM envelopes read them from here via
registry_license(), so a licence is corrected in one place.
Note what is absent and why. There is no Gujarat state tier to inherit -
every prior city arrived on top of an already-worked state (TNGIS, KWRIS,
MPCB, TGPCB, WBPCB). Surat is first contact with GWRDC, GPCB and the
Gujarat WRD, so all of these entries are new rather than reused.
The flood-chain source is tier 0 and daily because it is the only one on
this list that cannot be recovered if missed: SMC publishes a rolling
~10-reading window with no archive, no dated URL and no API.

sources.license: Surat Municipal Corporation public feed; no explicit licence stated - cited with attribution as the corporation's own operational record
sources.notes: Five tables: Ukai dam level/inflow/outflow, weir-cum-causeway level/outflow, zone-wise rainfall, season total, and five khadis each with a published Danger Level. SMC attributes the dam and weir rows to the Irrigation Dept / Collector Office. ROLLING WINDOW: history exists only from the first scrape and can never be backfilled.

sources.license: public Surat Municipal Corporation data; open WMS, GetCapabilities declares no fees and no access constraints, no explicit licence stated - cited with attribution
sources.notes: ~390 layers, the richest municipal GIS found on the platform. CONTRACT: GetMap and GetFeatureInfo (application/vnd.ogc.gml) work; WFS is DISABLED (IEG Code 1027) and GML carries gml:Box only, so attributes and rendered tiles are available but vector geometry is NOT. Enabling WFS is the open ask to SMC.

sources.publisher: Surat Municipal Corporation (hosted by CSE India)
sources.license: Surat Municipal Corporation publication (presented at a public CSE convening), cited with attribution
sources.refreshMethod: manual re-extraction on a new edition
sources.notes: Dated 8 Mar 2024. SMC's own figures for 11 STPs (1,726.50 MLD), 3 TTPs (164 MLD in, 115 MLD out, 249 industrial units), 330 MLD total reuse itemised across 11 uses, Rs 496.23 Cr cumulative revenue to Jan-2024, tariff Rs 18.20/KL (2014) to Rs 36.2/KL, and dated targets of 70% by 2030 and 100% by 2035. PREFER THESE over press figures, which report Rs 340 Cr / Rs 140 Cr annually and disagree with the corporation.

sources.license: Surat Municipal Corporation publication, cited with attribution
sources.notes: STALE BY ITS OWN LABEL: the page states 980 MLD gross daily supply, 1,300 MLD installed works capacity and 95% piped coverage, all explicitly for 2015. Infrastructure description only; never a current number.

sources.license: Surat Municipal Corporation publication, cited with attribution
sources.notes: 134 ward rows with area and census population 1961-2011, showing the city growing from 8 km2 (12 wards) to 462.149 km2 across six annexations including the June 2020 extension. The spine of the Origins narrative.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Smart Cities Mission (Surat) via data.gov.in
sources.notes: Three releases. D53 monthly total supply Jan-2018 to Dec-2021 (48 real points) and D52 property connection coverage 2018-19 to 2020-21 are usable. D42 gives per-sub-ward CAPACITY across 233 sub-wards, 8 zones, 1,342 MLD. DO NOT PUBLISH the derived columns: D53's 'Losses including NRW' is exactly 20.0000% of total on all 48 rows while 'actual supplied' equals total (self-contradictory), and D42's 'domestic consumption' is exactly 0.750000 x capacity on all 233 rows. Both are assumptions presented as measurements.

sources.license: Government of India publication, cited with attribution
sources.refreshMethod: manual; same extraction pipeline as the Hyderabad Musi rebuild
sources.notes: Annual national NWMP compilation. SIX editions ingested (2019-2024) giving 45 station-years: seven Gujarat Tapi stations forming an upstream-to-sea profile (Ukai, Mandavi, Bardoli/Kakrapar, Kathore, Surat u/s, Rander, ONGC Hazira) plus the Mindhola at Sachin from 2022. LAYOUT VARIES BY EDITION: major-river tables lead each row with the station code, while the 2022 medium/minor table trails it, so the extractor also matches on a unique name keyword. Editions are sometimes served truncated by CPCB and must be re-downloaded, not skipped.

sources.publisher: Space Applications Centre (ISRO), National Wetland Atlas hydrological layer
sources.license: Government of India publication, cited with attribution
sources.notes: Gujarat statewide layer; 3,401 polygons fall in the Surat district box, with 17 more contributed by OpenStreetMap where the national-scale atlas missed a body. Carries level_i/level_ii, area_ha, turbidity, aquatic vegetation and wetcode. THIN SEMANTICS: level_iii and l4type are empty for every Surat feature and only 34 carry a name. The wetcode's first two digits ARE decodable and are decoded (1/2 = Inland/Coastal, 1/2 = Natural/Man-made), verified exact against level_i/level_ii across all 18,279 Gujarat features; the leaf digits are not, because no primary SAC code table was obtained and a secondary summary of it contradicted the data.

sources.license: Government of India publication, cited with attribution
sources.refreshMethod: manual export, filtered to District == SURAT
sources.notes: About 65 Surat-district stations, ~6,500 readings, 1970-2026. THREE TRAPS: the export filenames misstate their own date ranges (the file named 1991_2020 holds Aug-Dec 2020; 2026_2030 holds Jan-May 2026), the Block column is '-' for every Surat row so block joins are impossible from this export, and telemetry sign convention is mixed - apply the per-station sign rule before rendering.

Named river and stream ways in the Surat box. GAP: OSM names none of the five khadis SMC monitors against published danger levels, so the creeks central to the flood chain have no geometry. SMC's GIS holds a creek layer but serves WMS only, with WFS disabled, so its geometry cannot be redistributed.
